To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a shaft-hub press-fitted joint subjected to couples or radial forces is prone to shaft-hub incipience separation when the radial force or the couple applied to the hub is larger than a certain value.

the shaft-hub press-fit subjected to couples and/or to radial forces can be analytically evaluated, and that the shaft-hubs detachment can be avoided if the initial shaft-hubs interference is large enough.
the shaft-hub press-fitting subjected to couples and/or to radial forces is a complex problem that cannot be addressed with the usual beam-like models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical evaluation of the shaft–hub incipient detachment under two different loading conditions.

the theoretical evaluation of the shaft and hub geometry, of the shaft-hubs interference, and of some elastic constants, which determine the loading conditions inducing an undesired incipient detachment between shaft and hub.
the evaluation of a critical loading for shaft-hub press fits subjected to couples and/or radial loads.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the shaft-hub contact model is very well represented by a Winkler foundation, and that the beam-like analytical model is able to provide an accurate and reliable estimate of the shaft-huber incipient detachment loading.

the beam-like model, which has the merit of simplicity and is therefore suitable for design purposes, can be used for a correct prediction of the loading inducing the incipient detachment, provided the shaft-hub interference is small and the shaft-hub elastic constants are similar.
the shaft-hub incipience of detachment is analytically determined in terms of a simple beam-like model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the two non-axisymmetric loadings considered here, the shaft-hub incipience of detachment is predicted with a good degree of accuracy.

, when the shaft-hub contact surface is not perfectly smooth and the contact is modelled by means of a Winkler foundation, the analytical evaluation of the incipient detachment loading can be obtained in closed form, with an acceptable accuracy.

, when the shaft-hub press-fit is loaded by a central radial force P or by a couple C, the shaft-hub contact may be modelled as an enhanced elastic beam, and an analytical expression of the critical value of P or C inducing the incipient shaft-hub detachment may be derived.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loading leading to incipient shaft-hub detachment is a function of the elastic constants and the initial shaft-hubberse.

a shaft-hub interference of 10% of the shaft diameter can be safely withstood by shaft-hubs with a length-to-diameter ratio of 1.5, provided the shaft is subjected to a maximum axial stress of 0.3 GPa.
the analytical model is capable of predicting the shaft-hub incipience of detachment with a maximum error lower than 5%, and it is therefore suitable for the preliminary design stage.
